headline: Masked diffusion and contrastive objectives extend genomic language models
label: Biological Sequence Language Models
summary: Recent preprints and publications benchmark and extend DNA, RNA, and pathogen-focused language models across sequence understanding and classification tasks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the transfer of language modeling objectives and architectures to nucleotide and pathogen-related sequence tasks. Influ-BERT applies domain-adaptive genomic pretraining to influenza A virus research. NyxBind uses contrastive learning across TFBS types to sharpen genomic language model embeddings, reporting a 4.71 point MCC gain over DNABERT2 across 159 tasks. D3LM applies masked discrete diffusion to Nucleotide Transformer v2, unifying bidirectional DNA understanding and generation. The RNA benchmark evaluates 21 RNA language models with DNA LM controls on structure prediction, classification, and mutational fitness under zero-shot conditions. The pathogen-disease study tests open-source LLMs at 4B to 70B parameters on binary classification of PubMed abstracts. What is new is the use of masked diffusion and contrastive objectives on genomic models, alongside standardized zero-shot comparison across RNA and DNA language models. Pathogen-specific work is limited to Influ-BERT and the pathogen-disease benchmark; the remaining items address general sequence tasks.
